C01.title_en: Acquire and memorize the knowledge, even new knowledge, needed to monitor and carry out complex, multidisciplinary projects.

C02.title_en: Organize theoretical and experimental knowledge to identify and link the various components of projects, and interact effectively with all those involved.

C03.title_en: Draw up specifications to characterize a problem, and design solutions, systems and products, using practical and critical thinking skills.

C04.title_en: Undertake innovative work with a view to breaking new ground, using engineering tools and methods and digital agility.

C05.title_en: Collaborate scientifically in research and development activities.

C06.title_en: Search for and extract relevant information from a variety of qualified sources. Use critical thinking skills to adapt information to the problem at hand.

C07.title_en: Develop a posture of industrial or service activity pilot, mastering customer awareness, cost, quality and lead time. Integrate the company's strategy and be a force for responsible proposals and initiatives.

C08.title_en: Manage teams with a view to collective success, respecting the common good. Pay attention to health and safety issues. Mobilize your ability to influence and position yourself accordingly in your professional environment.

C09.title_en: Integrate the challenges and needs of the planet and humanity into every aspect of your actions, in line with the motto “Think globally, act locally”. Act according to the principles of integral ecology.

C10.title_en: Contribute to the dynamics of the team project by approaching each person with benevolence, without preconceived ideas, using communication skills and leadership to mobilize.

C11.title_en: Be committed and enterprising on a corporate, social and personal level, initiating change, measuring the risks and bringing it to fruition.

C12.title_en: Exercise one's profession as an engineer, in both English and French, in an intercultural situation, thanks to one's knowledge of cultural systems and experiences.

C13.title_en: Discern and refine one's desires, identify one's value system, and take responsibility for one's professional, personal and societal choices, in order to give meaning to one's actions.

MIA_PP1.description: Sequence in brief In this project, students will develop and program a drone delivery system using a drone simulation, providing hands-on experience with real-world applications. They will learn to handle user inputs, apply basic operations, and select appropriate variable types to manage data. By implementing loops, conditions, and functions, they will control the drone's automated tasks and integrate external libraries like GPS for accurate navigation. The project also emphasizes writing clear, well-commented code and delivering an error-free solution. Students will use flowcharts to visualize their algorithm and ensure their drone simulation operates smoothly from start to finish.

teachers.name: Nada BEN ABDESSALAM

MIA_PP2.description: Sequence in brief In this semester 2 project, students will develop a mobile application to guide a drone, with a special focus on implementing a "follow me" feature. Through this project, students will learn to send HTTP requests to a web server, enabling real-time interaction between the app and the drone. This hands-on activity combines mobile app development with web-based communication, providing students with valuable experience in both programming and drone control technology.

MIA_PP3.description: Sequence in brief In this project, students will embark on an exciting journey to build a boat autopilot using low-cost components, fostering hands-on learning through experimentation. MIA_PP4.description: Sequence in brief In this project, students will delve into automatic control systems to manage a boat's speed and direction effectively. They will gain theoretical knowledge while exploring the principles of dynamic system control. The focus will be on understanding the concepts of system feedback, representing dynamic systems through block diagrams, and synthesizing basic controllers like PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controllers. Students will implement these controllers in a practical context, adapting actuator behavior based on sensor inputs.
